correctness.rationale: For every n≥4, each of the 2n generating tetrahedra has a unique free opposite triangle, and each of the 2n remaining rim-path triangles has a unique free distance-two rim edge. After exactly 4n elementary pairs, the residual face set equals the union of n tetrahedral boundaries on cycle squares. Their only pairwise overlaps are consecutive rung edges. A connected 2n-edge base graph F has one loop and meets every tetrahedral boundary in a contractible three-edge path containing all its overlaps, proving the integral wedge S1 ∨ n S2 by homotopy pushouts. The oriented two-sphere generators are permuted with positive sign by rotation and reflection; square-boundary relations give rotation + and reflection − in H1. Standalone verify.py executed and confirmed every local face/collapse/intersection/sign identity n=4..100 and independent raw mod-two homology n=4..16. The symbolic proof, not finite extrapolation, supports all n.

originality.rationale: The primary closed-neighborhood paper gives general equivalences, fundamental groups, and an example for Cartesian products of complete graphs, none of which computes this Möbius-ladder family. A complete public result on the same ladders concerns the distinct open Lovász neighborhood complex, whose parity-dependent annulus/Möbius-band types do not imply the present closed-neighborhood homotopy type. The closest closed Čech prism theorem requires an untwisted Cartesian product H square K2, which does not include the half-twisted Möbius ladder. The finite index and owner claim checks found no identical or stronger applicable result. A separate independence/perfect-matching paper treats different complexes. Claims of absolute novelty are not made.
residual_risks: Global novelty cannot be established from accessible indexed records: a prior equivalent calculation under an unexpected name may exist.
The complete latest Agarwal–Basak manuscript was inaccessible, so any incidental calculations outside its described objects could not be verified.
The homology action is proved, not an equivariant homotopy decomposition; no statement is made about n=3 or higher Čech scales.

value.rationale: The canonical Möbius-ladder family is a natural and current object in graph-complex topology. The theorem resolves its complete closed-neighborhood integral homotopy type at every nonexceptional size, with an explicit uniform collapse explaining the sphere necklace and a full integral dihedral homology action. It exhibits a nontrivial open-versus-closed distinction: the previously classified open complex switches between an annulus and two Möbius bands, while the closed complex always has one circle and n two-spheres. The nearest untwisted-prism result does not imply a twisted-ladder theorem; this is not just a finite numeric extension or a known table restatement.
